title: Biophilic Design in the Built Environment to Improve Well-Being: A Systematic Review of Practices
review_question: What is the existing evidence concerning indoor environments featuring biophilic design? What is the evidence of the implementations of biophilic design in workplaces and residential buildings? How can applications be integrated into a holistic conceptual model to be considered in sustainable building design?
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: Inclusion: original and peer-reviewed articles in English or Arabic; studies focused on applications and implications (not definitions/principles); qualitative, quantitative, or mixed-method studies. Exclusion: studies not related to architecture/interior design; sources outside the 2008-February 2018 timeframe.

findings.antecedent: employing biophilic practices in the built environment
findings.consequent: physiological, psychological, and cognitive well-being outcomes; productivity; creativity; comfort; mood states; stress; health complaints; collaborative environment; satisfaction; ecological and sustainable built environment
findings.quote: The results of employing biophilic practices were positive physiological, psychological, and cognitive well-being outcomes that boost productivity, creativity and comfort; ameliorate mood states; reduce stress; lessen health complaints; foster a collaborative environment; increase satisfaction, and promote the ecological and sustainable built environment.

synthesis_conclusions: Biophilic interior design is a rapidly evolving approach and a sustainable design strategy that promotes nature-health relationships by mediating between nature and the indoor environment.
The twenty-four attributes of biophilic design and their three related experiences are partly adopted in empirical studies and explored in descriptive studies.
A conceptual model emerged with three themes (design and building management, occupants' needs, and technology) allied with two poles (sustainability and biophilic interior design).
Management, especially in office buildings, should prioritize biophilic design to address the costs of unsustainable workplaces on social and human capital.
Occupant comfort and satisfaction in various building types can be enhanced, necessitating repeatability and measurability of design applications.
Technology has the potential to drive markets toward high-quality, sustainable buildings.
evidence_gaps: Little research exists on how all 24 biophilic attributes work together or how to measure and quantify their human, environmental, and economic outcomes.
Future research should focus on the 'Indirect Experience of Nature' attributes (A9, A11, A12, A13, A16, A17, A18) for residential buildings.
Future research should focus on the 'Indirect Experience of Nature' attributes (A11, A16) for workplaces.
An existing gap in Arabic evidence documents was identified (only one documented was found and excluded).
risk_of_bias_assessment: Quality assessment criteria (Transparency, Accuracy, Completeness) were used to minimize the risk of bias in the review. The systematic review is considered low risk of bias, despite primary studies potentially having high risk, because the review appropriately assessed and considered this risk.
limitations: The study was limited by a ten-year time frame (2008-February 2018), despite an increasing pool of evidence.
Only workplaces and residential buildings were included in the second phase of the review.
The simultaneous search across four large databases was time-consuming, particularly in avoiding duplicates.

The matrix analysis, performed independently by two researchers, was time-consuming due to the need for exact agreement on coding Kellert's 24 attributes, some of which are close in meaning or share features.
Not all 24 attributes of biophilic design were reported by included studies.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Exposure to natural environments or elements can restore directed attention and reduce mental fatigue, thereby improving cognitive performance.
Exposure to natural environments can lead to physiological and psychological stress reduction, promoting feelings of calm and well-being.

mechanism_chain.description: Biophilic practices in the built environment lead to well-being outcomes through perceptual engagement, positive affective responses, and subsequent cognitive and physiological restoration.
